headline: A receiver class with a franchise player at the top
summary: This is a wide receiver draft. Nine of the top 24 rookies on the board are receivers, led by Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, the clearest 1.01 in years, with Indiana's Charlie Becker, Rutgers' KJ Duff and Texas's Cam Coleman behind him. If you need a receiver, this is the year to have an early pick.

Running back is the next strongest spot. Florida's Jadan Baugh is the best of the backs, and Missouri's Ahmad Hardy, Ole Miss's Kewan Lacy and Georgia's Nate Frazier give the class real depth, though Hardy and Lacy carry injury questions into the spring.

Quarterback is the story that matters most for us. FBP goes superflex in 2027, so a starting QB can fill two lineup spots, and this class has real ones: Drew Mestemaker, Darian Mensah and CJ Carr have all climbed this fall, with Dante Moore and Arch Manning close behind. Expect them to go early, maybe ahead of a receiver or back you'd have taken in a one-QB year. Tight end is thin. Trey'Dez Green and Jamari Johnson are the only early-round names.

profiles.name: Jeremiah Smith
profiles.text: A 6-4, 223-pound receiver who has done everything since the day he arrived: 76 catches for 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns as a freshman on a national title team, then 87 for 1,243 and 12 and a unanimous All-American nod in 2025. Two-time Big Ten Receiver of the Year, now Ohio State's career leader. Hands, size, speed and route craft are all elite.

profiles.name: Jadan Baugh
profiles.text: The best back in the class opened 2026 with 600 yards and 11 touchdowns in four games, over seven yards a carry and 100 yards every week. Patient behind the line, and the receiving role is growing. Boards compare his style to Le'Veon Bell's.

profiles.name: Charlie Becker
profiles.text: Indiana's clear No. 1 receiver and one of PFF's top 15 wideouts nationally. A former state-champion hurdler, and it shows in his body control on the ball in the air. The best bet to be the second receiver off the board.

profiles.name: Drew Mestemaker
profiles.text: Led the nation in passing yards at North Texas in 2025, then transferred to Oklahoma State and beat No. 6 Oregon with 317 yards passing and 109 rushing. The legs are what make him interesting for fantasy, and in superflex he's a top-five rookie pick; the Air Raid numbers need a grain of salt.

profiles.name: Ahmad Hardy
profiles.tag: All-American back, back on the field
profiles.text: An All-American in 2025, he missed the first two months of 2026 recovering from an offseason leg injury and made his season debut on Nov. 1 against Arkansas. How he looks over the final stretch will decide whether he stays a first-round rookie pick.

profiles.name: Darian Mensah
profiles.text: Climbed from outside the top 35 in September into the top tier, tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception at Miami. The question scouts ask: how much of it is a short, quick-throw offense.

profiles.name: Kewan Lacy
profiles.text: Scored 24 touchdowns at Ole Miss in 2025. This year has been a fight with his body: a lower-leg injury, shoulder trouble and a dislocation against Texas that cost him a game. At 205 pounds, durability is the knock.

profiles.name: CJ Carr
profiles.text: Notre Dame's starter beat Mensah and then-No. 1 Miami head to head this fall, and NFL scouts have taken notice. A pocket passer more than a runner, so his fantasy ceiling rides on where he lands, but in a superflex league a starting job alone makes him a first-round rookie pick.

profiles.name: KJ Duff
profiles.text: A 6-6, 225-pound receiver who moves like a smaller one. He accounts for nearly half of Rutgers' receiving yards and more than half of its receiving touchdowns. Built to win in the end zone.

profiles.name: Cam Coleman
profiles.text: The talent is obvious: a deep threat with first-round tools. The production hasn't matched it at Texas (23 catches, 409 yards and 7 touchdowns through eight games), which is why he slid from third on some boards in September.
